High-frequency traders like Jane Street and Hudson River Trading are now racing each other for AI computing power. The biggest firms are spending billions on cloud contracts, startups, and their own data centers, Bloomberg reports. Part of the reason is that they increasingly rely on machine learning to predict market moves.

One executive estimates that compute spending is now ten to twenty times higher than it was before ChatGPT launched. XTX Markets is building a data center in Finland, and Jane Street runs one in Texas with more than 4,000 Nvidia GPUs. Hudson River spends $1 billion a year on AI, according to AI chief Iain Dunning, and signed a multiyear deal with CoreWeave. Jane Street went a different route. It invested $1 billion directly in CoreWeave and committed $6 billion to its computing services.

Jane Street also led a funding round for chip startup Etched and became the first customer for its AI chip, which is supposed to deliver more performance by running at a lower voltage. According to Bloomberg, the industry sees rising costs and fast-aging chips as real risks. Executives like Jan Boomaars, CEO of Amsterdam-based high-frequency trader Optiver, still think doing nothing is more dangerous.

translation.html:
Jane Street 和 Hudson River Trading 等高频交易公司如今正竞相争夺 AI 算力。据彭博社报道，规模最大的公司正斥资数十亿美元，投入云服务合同、初创企业和自建数据中心。部分原因在于，它们越来越依赖机器学习来预测市场走势。

一位高管估计，如今的算力支出已是 ChatGPT 推出前的十到二十倍。XTX Markets 正在芬兰建设一座数据中心，Jane Street 则在得克萨斯州运营着一座配备超过 4,000 块英伟达 GPU 的数据中心。据 Hudson River 的 AI 负责人 Iain Dunning 介绍，该公司每年在 AI 上花费 10 亿美元，并与 CoreWeave 签订了一份多年期协议。Jane Street 选择了另一条路线，直接向 CoreWeave 投资 10 亿美元，并承诺投入 60 亿美元使用其计算服务。

Jane Street 还领投了芯片初创企业 Etched 的一轮融资，并成为其 AI 芯片的首位客户。这款芯片预计能通过在更低电压下运行来提供更高性能。据彭博社报道，业内认为，成本上涨和芯片迅速过时是切实存在的风险。但总部位于阿姆斯特丹的高频交易公司 Optiver 的首席执行官 Jan Boomaars 等高管仍认为，按兵不动更加危险。
